rationale.conceptual: MSM is an established but specialized method. The agent must correctly derive beam cross-section, moduli, build honeycomb lattices for different chiralities, assemble global matrices, condense, and solve eigenproblems for many configurations. Several interacting components and a moderate amount of mathematical translation are required; it is not a trivial textbook operation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has several sequential stages: compute beam properties, generate lattice coordinates, assemble matrices, condense, solve eigenvalues, handle strain updates, and loop over geometries/aspect ratios/strains. While the overall workflow is linear, building the atomistic models and managing the eigenvalue solution for many cases adds structural complexity beyond a simple script. Standard libraries (NumPy, SciPy sparse) suffice, and I/O is straightforward CSV writing.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing molecular structural mechanics (MSM) to simulate vibration of graphene sheets under strain. The method is non-trivial: it involves translating force constants into beam properties, constructing atomistic lattice geometries, assembling large stiffness/mass matrices, applying boundary conditions, performing static condensation, and solving eigenvalue problems. While formulas are given, correct implementation demands careful engineering and domain knowledge. The pipeline is multi-step but can be executed with standard numerical libraries. Resource needs are modest (CPU, few GB RAM).

compute_estimate.reasoning: SLGS models up to ~14 nm side length lead to matrices of several thousand degrees of freedom. Sparse matrix assembly and eigenvalue solution on CPU is feasible with a few GB of RAM. No external datasets; all constants are inline.
